data.title: Click-linking: a cell-compatible protein crosslinking method based on click chemistry
data.projectDescription: We developed a novel approach to in situ crosslinking mass spectrometry (XL-MS) where the reaction is split into two sequential and orthogonal coupling events. The method involves pre-stabilization of the proteome using a fixation protocol, followed by a two-step process that begins with extensive labeling of surface-available lysines with click-chemistry compatible reagents modified with NHS Esters. The second step involves the copper-catalyzed azide-alkyne cycloaddition (CuAAC) reaction of the installed precursors, which generates crosslinks with high efficiency. We observed approximately a 20-fold increase in protein-protein interactions detected by this approach when compared to standard DSS crosslinkers, and our Click-linking strategy even outperformed enrichable crosslinkers such as PhoX.
data.sampleProcessingProtocol: Human cells (A549) were grown on 10cm dishes to 80% confluency, then fixed with 4% formaldehyde in 1x PBS buffer and permeabilized with 0.1% Triton-X-100. Cells were washed and simultaneously labeled with 1mM of 2,5-dioxopyrrolidin-1-yl 3-(prop-2-ynyloxy)propanoate (Reagent 1) and 1mM of 2,5-Dioxopyrrolidin-1-yl) 6-azidohexanoate (Reagent 2) for 60min. Reaction was quench, excess reagent washed out, and, for the crosslinking samples, cells were incubated with click-catalysts (CuSO4, BTTES and sodium ascorbate). Click-chemistry reaction was quenched, excess catalysts were washed then cells were collected and lysed. Samples crosslinked with DSS and PhoX were used as points of comparison, and A549 cells treated the same as above were incubated with 1mM of each crosslinker. Proteins were reduced with 10mM DTT at 52 °C for 30min, alkylated with 40mM CAA at 25 °C for another 30min, then cleaned up using the SP3 protocol, followed by overnight digestion with trypsin. Peptides were desalted using C18 Ziptips for single injection samples or using Pierce Peptide Desalting Spin Columns for fractionated samples. Fractionation was carried out using High pH Reverse Phase chromatography. PhoX samples were enriched using Fe-NTA magnetic beads prior to High pH fractionation, while the larger Click-linking sample was submitted to Size-exclusion fractionation as an attempt to enrich for crosslinks. LC-MS analysis was performed using a Vanquish Neo HPLC coupled to a nano-ESI source of an Orbitrap Ascend (crosslinking samples) or an Orbitrap Astral (few non-crosslinking samples) from ThermoFisher Scientific. Samples were injected into a 300μm x 5mm PepMap Neo Trap cartridge (C18, 5μm particle size, 100Å pore size, Thermo Scientific) and reverse-phase separated on an EASY-Spray 75μm x 50cm PepMap HPLC column (C18, 2μm particle size, 100Å pore size, ThermoFisher Scientific) with a 180 minute gradient (crosslinking samples) or 120min gradient (non-crosslinking samples). MS/MS parameters are as follows: m/z range of 375-1800, charge-state selection 4-8+, MS1 resolution 120,000, MS2 resolution 30,000, normalized collision energy for stepped-HCD fragmentation at 27, 30, and 33%.
data.dataProcessingProtocol: Monovalent labeling efficiency was accessed using MSFragger inside FragPipe v22.0. For every sample, we performed an OpenMod search to confirm the expected mass shifts caused by our labeling strategies, followed by the LFQ-MBR workflow to investigate the quantitative proportion of labeled versus unlabeled peptides and thus estimating reaction performance. The LFQ-MBR search routine was performed against the full UniProt Human proteome database with the following parameters: cysteine carbamidomethylation (m = +57.021465 Da) as fixed modification; methionine oxidation (m = +15.9949 Da) and N-termini acetylation (m = +42.0106 Da) as variable modifications; 10ppm for precursor mass tolerance; 15ppm for fragment mass tolerance; trypsin as enzyme for protein digestion with 3 allowed missed cleavages. The mass shifts corresponding to the reagent modification were adjusted for every molecule as follows: Reagent 1 (Δm = 110.0366 Da), Reagent 2 (Δm = 139.0745 Da), DBCO-Capped-Azide (Δm = 444.1798 Da). IonQuant was used for label-free quantitation and each mass spec run was processed individually. Crosslinking data analysis was performed using pLink 2.3.11. Parameters used were mostly default, but including; carbamidomethylation of cysteines ((m = +57.021 Da) as fixed modification; oxidation of methionine (Δm = +15.995 Da) as variable modification; 5ppm for precursor and 10ppm for fragment mass tolerance. Data was searched against the full UniProt Human proteome databases at 5% false discovery rate (FDR) at the spectrum level. Crosslink (Δm = +249.111 Da) and Monolink (only one monolink is allowed on pLink, we selected the more abundant Reagent 1 at Δm = +110.037 Da) modifications were added for the clicked products, with specificity towards Lysine residues and protein N-termini. pLink already has the DSS crosslinker set up in the default configuration, and for PhoX modifications were manually added (Δm = + 209.972 Da for crosslink, Δm = + 227.982 Da for monolink). The results from pLink were searched against the STRING human protein interaction database (v12.0, retrieved March 2024) and mapped into protein structures using CLAUDIO (v1.0).
